text:
Ada: Heads-up — drafting a set of short competitor scripts for SDRs and AE playbooks. Need one vs cloud AI platforms, one vs LLM API providers, and a tiny note vs infra vendors. Goal: 30–60s call opener + 3 rebut bullets each.
Ben: Awesome. Can we fold in the recent benchmark numbers and a latency/cost soundbite? Sales wants something punchy for intros.
Frances: I have a two-line benchmark we'll own: "Typical customer configs saw 35–55% lower per-token unit cost using Redwood batching + KV cache vs unmanaged cloud endpoints (same models)". Also: "P95 gen latency comparable or better on dedicated pools for 512-token workloads." Happy to shorten.
Charlie: +1 from product. Add a single line about graceful fallback policies (route to cheaper variant) — customers care about reliability.
Ellen: For infra vendor comparisons, keep it ops-focused: control plane vs bring-your-own-runtime tradeoffs, e.g., we handle quantization profiles and ops telemetry out of the box.
Ben: Sales ask: can we get a one-liner for the top 3 competitor claims and one-sentence counters? Example format: "Claim: X\nCounter: Y"
Frances: Drafts below. Please iterate.

Frances: Claim: "Cloud vendors are fastest because they own the hardware"
Counter: "Redwood’s serving runtime and smart kernel selection deliver consistent P95s across clouds and dedicated pools; customers see predictable latency without lock-in."

Frances: Claim: "LLM API providers have ready-made models and fine-tuning"
Counter: "We match model capabilities via model catalog + vetted variants and provide rollout tooling and function calling for production use cases — plus cost controls (batching, cache, quantization)."

Frances: Claim: "Infra vendors give you full control and the best performance"
Counter: "If you want control without building ops from scratch: Redwood gives per-route telemetry, KV/prefix caching, and autoscaling controls as a managed option or private deploy. Lower operational burden + predictable economics."

Ada: This is great. Can we compress each to one line for the battlecard front? And add one measurable stat per counter where possible (like the 35–55% cost stat).
Charlie: I'll make a condensed front-side version. Also recommend a 1-slide appendix with the benchmark graph and methodology notes.
Ben: Webinar tie-in: schedule a 20-min live mini-demo + 10-min panel for customers asking about migration. Would be good to use these scripts as role-play in the demo (SDR <> buyer).
Ada: Webinar draft page: May 18 — "Serving for scale: balancing cost, latency, and reliability". Panelists: Frances (bench), Charlie (product), Maya (customer). Need a short speaker brief with these counters.
Ellen: For inbound routing, add recommended intent tags: pricing, latency, private-deploy. Route pricing leads to growth, private-deploy to AE enterprise queue.
Ben: I'll update the routing rules after we finalize the battlecard front. Low-lift: add a keyword rule for "quantization" -> support docs + AE.
Frances: Quick note: benchmark doc link: https://docs.google.com/example-benchmarks (internal) — includes methodology and raw runs. Use only the condensed stat on external-facing content.
Ada: Action items: Charlie condense front lines (due EOD), Ben update routing + one-liners for SDRs (tomorrow), Frances trim benchmark stat and share approved phrasing, Ellen craft ops blurb for infra vendor slide. I'll collate and make a 1-pager. 
deploy-bot: Reminder: marketing-docs pipeline lint passed for new fight-cards folder. :white_check_mark:
Ben: Perfect. Quick win: once Charlie shares condensed lines, I'll bake them into the outbound email template and a 3-line pitch for website FAQ.
Ada: Thanks team — we'll iterate in this thread. :thumbsup:
